name: Belmond Villa San Michele
positioning: Former 15th-century monastery in the hills above Florence, reopened in 2026 as Villa San Michele, a Belmond Hotel
best_for: Travelers who want a historic hillside retreat above Florence
Food lovers who want several restaurants on site
Couples and adults looking for a grown-up atmosphere

facts.text: The hotel began life as a monastery in the 15th century.
Villa San Michele is perched in the hills above Florence, overlooking the Arno Valley.
The terraced gardens were originally tended by monks.
Ristorante San Michele serves traditional slow food creations.
A complimentary shuttle runs to Florence city centre.
The hotel is a 30-minute drive from Florence Airport.
Executive chef Alessandro Cozzolino oversees the three restaurants.
Guests can order bistecca alla Fiorentina at the hotel.
Footpaths wind through the wooded grounds that climb the hill behind the hotel.

highlights.text: The hotel's facade is attributed to the School of Michelangelo.
The hotel has a panoramic, heated outdoor swimming pool.
Antesi serves sophisticated Italian dining with panoramic views.
The hotel re-opened in May 2026 after an 18-month renovation.
Off-site experiences for guests include exploring the local artisan scene and learning about paper marbling.

considerations.text: Children are welcome, but the atmosphere is quite grown-up.
Evenings can be chilly outside the warm season.
WhataHotel notes the hillside location requires transportation to reach Florence city centre.

sources.title: Condé Nast Traveler: Villa San Michele, A Belmond Hotel, Florence
